subject: general
question: According to the 2011 census which city of India has the second largest population?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the 2011 census, Delhi is the second most populous city in India after Mumbai.
 
• Delhi had a population of approximately 11 million in 2011, making it a major urban hub in India.
 
• Delhi is also the capital city of India and has significant political, cultural, and historical importance.
 
• The National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi includes New Delhi, which is the seat of all three branches of the Government of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **2011 Census of India**

 
 
• The 2011 Census of India was the 15th National Census since 1871.
 
• It was conducted by the Census Commissioner of India and was the largest administrative exercise in the world.
 
• The census provides demographic data such as population size, distribution, density, and various socio-economic indicators.
 
• The data collected helps in policy formulation, planning, and administration in various sectors like health, education, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Population Density**
 
 
• Population density is calculated as the number of people per unit area, typically per square kilometer.
 
• High population density areas often face challenges such as congestion, pollution, and strain on infrastructure and resources.
 
• Delhi has one of the highest population densities among Indian cities, which impacts its urban planning and resource management.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization in India**
 
 
• Urbanization refers to the increasing population in urban areas compared to rural areas.
 
• Factors contributing to urbanization include economic opportunities, better infrastructure, and improved living standards.
 
• Delhi is a prime example of rapid urbanization, attracting people from various regions for employment and better living conditions.
 
 
 
• **National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi**
 
 
• The NCT of Delhi includes not just Delhi city but also New Delhi, the capital of India.
 
• New Delhi hosts the central administrative functions of the Indian government, including the Parliament House, Rashtrapati Bhavan, and the Supreme Court.
 
• The NCT is divided into multiple districts and is governed by its own legislative assembly and Chief Minister.
